assumptions: Synthetic handler_effect transcribed from cgi-io main_upload; C, not ucode

cgi-io main_upload requires session.access scope=cgi-io object=upload function=write AND session.access scope=file object=canonicalize_path(filename) function=write. A cgi-io grant without the file-write grant cannot authorize.
cgi-io upload failures use response() which prints Status 200 with a JSON failure body, not failure(403). http_status stays 200; outcome distinguishes invalid_request / upload_denied / path_denied.
Filename is canonicalized before the file ACL check so a '../' suffix cannot match /etc/luci-uploads/* while linkat/open resolves outside that prefix.
This oracle does not create tempfiles, chmod, or copy bytes
shellquote and basename are not sanitizers. canonicalize_path is a textual path normalizer, not a taint sanitizer.

unknowns: Live cgi-io, uhttpd, and rpcd were not executed; decisions are transcribed from pinned C and ACL JSON.
Multipart framing, boundary scanning, and temp-file copy/chmod are not modeled; this slice assumes already-decoded sessionid and filename fields.
cgi-download and cgi-exec are not emitted in this slice. cgi-backup stays on policy:cgi-backup-v1.
